section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The Geometric Meaning of a Matrix
section_1.content: Recall that a matrix acts as a machine that transforms a vector. We visualize this as a 2D grid morphing: matrix A transforms space by moving the basis vectors i and j. Emphasize that the columns of the matrix tell us exactly where i and j land.
section_1.example: A matrix [[0, -1], [1, 0]] acts as a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation of a character icon on a screen.

section_2.title: The Concept of Composition
section_2.content: Define 'composition' as applying transformations in sequence: first transformation B, then transformation A. Introduce the notation A(B(v)). Visually, this is a two-step process: an object is moved, then the result of that move is moved again.
section_2.example: Applying a 'Stretch' (Matrix B) to an image of a cat, followed by a 'Rotation' (Matrix A) of the stretched image.

section_3.title: Deriving the Matrix Product
section_3.content: Show that the composition A(B(v)) is equivalent to a single matrix C acting on v, where C = AB. Explain that to find the columns of C, we observe what happens to the basis vectors i and j after passing through B then A.
section_3.example: Trace the path of the 'i' vector: i goes to B's first column, then that new vector is multiplied by A. This explains why the order of multiplication follows column-by-column logic.

section_4.title: Visualizing Non-Commutativity
section_4.content: Explain why AB ≠ BA by demonstrating that 'Rotate then Stretch' results in a different final position than 'Stretch then Rotate'. Use a visual grid to show how the final orientation of shapes differs.
section_4.example: Rotating a robot arm by 90 degrees then extending it, vs. extending the arm then rotating the entire assembly.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Summarize that matrix multiplication is not just a calculation, but a 'shortcut' for combining transformations. By pre-calculating the product matrix, we turn two operations into one, saving computational power.
section_5.example: In a 3D video game engine, chaining hundreds of transformations (scaling, rotating, translating) into a single product matrix before rendering each frame.
